skill.name: image-inpainting
skill.description: Use RunComfy image inpainting models to remove, replace, or repair masked regions in still images with the runcomfy CLI.
skill.summary: Run mask-driven image inpainting and local image edits through RunComfy.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks, documented links, or model-selection prose rather than hidden execution. The real risks are scoped RunComfy CLI execution, disclosed outbound network use, local token storage, and contextual misuse around watermark removal.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution and remote processing
remediation.suggestion: Keep the allowed tool scope limited to runcomfy commands, require user-provided inputs, and disclose that images and masks are processed by RunComfy endpoints.

remediation.issue: API token stored in a hidden home-directory file
remediation.suggestion: Document token file permissions, recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for ephemeral environments, and warn users not to share the token file.
Require explicit confirmation that the user owns the image or has permission before assisting with watermark or rights-mark removal.

remediation.issue: Third-party image and mask URLs are untrusted inputs
remediation.suggestion: Use only URLs provided for the current task and avoid fetching or processing unrelated external media.

content.user_title: Edit Masked Image Regions with RunComfy
content.value_statement: Precise local image edits can be hard to route to the right model. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through mask-based inpainting with the RunComfy CLI.
actual_capabilities: Selects the Z-Image Turbo Inpainting endpoint when a mask image is available.
Shows runcomfy CLI commands for masked object removal and region replacement.
Explains required input fields such as image, mask_image, prompt, strength, and control_scale.
Routes no-mask edits to description-based image editing models.
Provides troubleshooting references for RunComfy CLI exit codes and authentication.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy account or token.
Requires source images and masks to be available as URLs for the documented workflow.
Does not create masks; users need external mask creation tools.
The skill is for still images, not video or canvas extension workflows.

use_cases.title: Repair product photos
use_cases.description: Replace a masked background or repair a small product-photo defect while preserving the product edges.

use_cases.title: Clean up creative assets
use_cases.description: Remove unwanted visible objects from a licensed asset when the edit is authorized and a mask is available.

use_cases.title: Prototype local image edits
use_cases.description: Test RunComfy inpainting model inputs, strength values, and output handling from a command-line workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Basic masked cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with existing image and mask URLs
prompt_templates.prompt: Inpaint this image using the provided mask URL. Remove the masked object and preserve everything outside the mask.

prompt_templates.title: Controlled background replacement
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate product or marketing image edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mask to replace only the background with a clean studio backdrop. Keep the subject shape, lighting, and colors unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Tune strength and preservation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced quality control for local edits
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose inpainting settings for a subtle repair. Explain the strength and control_scale values before running the RunComfy command.

prompt_templates.title: Route a no-mask edit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced fallback when only a text description is available
prompt_templates.prompt: I do not have a mask. Route this to a description-based edit model and preserve all unmentioned areas of the image.

output_examples.input: Remove a small masked object from a street photo and keep the surrounding sky consistent.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Z-Image Turbo Inpainting, prepares a RunComfy command with image and mask URLs, and recommends moderate strength for natural blending.

output_examples.input: Replace a masked product-photo background with light gray studio paper.
output: Uses high strength for full background replacement.
Keeps the product area outside the mask unchanged.

output_examples.input: Remove an object when no mask is available.
output_examples.output: The skill routes the request to a description-based image edit model and warns that pixel-level edges are less precise without a mask.

best_practices: Use only images and masks that the user explicitly provided or authorized.
Describe what must stay unchanged outside the mask in every prompt.
Start with lower strength for repairs and increase strength for full replacements.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to remove watermarks or rights marks without clear authorization.
Do not pass arbitrary third-party URLs unless the user confirms they are intended inputs.
Do not use description-based fallback when exact mask boundaries are required.

faq.question: Does this skill create the mask image?
faq.answer: No. It consumes an existing mask URL. Use a separate design or segmentation tool to create the mask.

faq.question: Which model is the default route?
faq.answer: The default route is Tongyi MAI Z-Image Turbo Inpainting when a mask is available.

faq.question: Can it work without a mask?
faq.answer: Yes, but it routes to description-based edit models. Those models are less precise for exact boundaries.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The RunComfy CLI sends jobs to RunComfy endpoints and downloads the generated result.

faq.question: Where are outputs saved?
faq.answer: The documented commands save generated files to the output directory passed to the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Is watermark removal allowed?
faq.answer: Only when the user has clear rights or authorization. Unauthorized removal can violate policy, contracts, or copyright rules.
